summary.suggested: The St. Louis Post-Dispatch reported that Tom Allen, one of Charley Mitchell's seconds, returned from Florida calling the Corbett-Mitchell fight a farce and predicting Corbett would beat Peter Jackson.

metadata.notes: Masthead: Sunday Morning, St. Louis Post-Dispatch, January 28, 1894, page 8.

facts.fact: Allen was one of Charley Mitchell's seconds in his fight with James J. Corbett in Florida, which Corbett won
Allen returned to St. Louis from Florida after the Corbett-Mitchell fight
Allen said Mitchell was outclassed and Corbett would have chopped him into ribbons
facts.quote: Mitchell was outclassed in every respect, and Corbett would have chopped him into ribbons in a few more rounds.

facts.fact: Allen predicted Corbett would beat Peter Jackson
facts.quote: Yes sir, I am thoroughly convinced this Californian can whip them all, including Peter Jackson and Ed Smith.

facts.fact: Allen prepared his ox-tail jelly to harden Mitchell's stomach for the Corbett fight

notes: Fight date inferred from 'Thursday' before the Sunday Jan. 28 paper (Jan. 25, 1894); the article names only Florida, not Jacksonville.
